card.title: Nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every periodic trend is the contest between **nuclear charge Z** (the proton count, the total pull) and **shielding σ** (inner electrons cancelling part of that pull); the score is **Z_eff = Z − σ**, the net pull an electron actually feels.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Z_eff = Z − σ - Slater contributions: same shell 0.35 (1s: 0.30); (n−1) shell 0.85; deeper 1.00 - Penetration order: s > p > d > f

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Z vs Z_eff:** Z is the total proton count and never changes with position; Z_eff is what a *particular* electron actually feels — quoting one where the other is asked loses the mark.  ·  **Same-shell shielding is weak (0.35):** that is the entire reason Z_eff rises across a period; treating all shielding as equal makes the trend disappear.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron after shielding by the intervening electrons."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Na (Z_eff ≈ +1) vs Cl (Z_eff ≈ +7)*** — same period, same shell, six protons' difference in net pull: Na gives its electron away, Cl grabs one more — the chemistry of table salt in two numbers.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: nuclear charge, effective nuclear charge (within Classification of Elements and Periodic Table).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Tug-of-War Inside Every Atom Every periodic trend — radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity, metallic character — is one contest: the **nuclear charge pulling electrons in** versus **inner-electron shielding pushing the outer experience out**. The score of that contest is the **effective nuclear charge (Z_eff)**.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Nuclear charge (Z) - **Z = number of protons** in the nucleus = the element's atomic number. - It is the true pull available: +Z on every electron (Coulomb attraction). ### 2.2 Shielding (screening) effect Inner-shell electrons sit **between** the nucleus and the valence electrons, repelling the outer electrons and **cancelling part of the nuclear pull**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Z_eff = Z − σ; across = up, down = flat." Same-shell shielders count little (0.35); inner shells count much (0.85/1.0). Name the electron you are computing for.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Define nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge with one example.** — **Nuclear charge (Z):** the total positive charge of the nucleus = proton count (Na: Z = 11). **Effective nuclear charge (Z_eff):** the net pull an electron actually feels after shielding by intervening electrons, Z_eff = Z − σ (Na's valence 3s…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Explain why Z_eff increases across a period but remains nearly constant down a group.** — **Across a period:** each added proton is matched by an electron in the **same shell**; same-shell electrons shield poorly (≈0.35 each), so the net pull on the valence shell grows (Na ≈ +1 → Cl ≈ +7).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Always pair the definition with one computed example (Na ≈ +1) — a bare definition rarely earns full 2m. Link Z_eff to the trend asked (radius/IE/EN) in the same sentence.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One tug-of-war explains every trend:** Z↑ pulling vs n↑/shielding pushing. Across a period the pull wins; down a group the shielding wins. All of topic 26 derives from this sentence.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Z = proton count; shielding σ = inner electrons' cancelling effect; Z_eff = Z − σ. Across a period Z_eff rises (poor same-shell shielding) → radius ↓, IE ↑, electronegativity ↑, metallic character ↓. Down a group Z_eff ≈ constant (new shell shields fully) → radius ↑, IE ↓, metallic character ↑.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Slater's rules (1930) remain the standard pencil-and-paper Z_eff estimate; modern Hartree–Fock calculations confirm the same period/group behaviour.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Using Slater's rules, estimate Z_eff for a valence electron of Li (Z = 3).** — The 2s¹ electron is shielded by the two 1s electrons (n−1 shell): σ = 2 × 0.85 = 1.7 → Z_eff = 3 − 1.7 = **+1.3** (simple estimate: 3 − 2 = +1).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): How does Z_eff account for the decrease in atomic radii across period 3?** — Na → Cl: electrons enter the same n = 3 shell while Z grows 11 → 17; same-shell shielding is weak, so Z_eff rises by ~6.…

Comparison Tables **Nuclear charge vs effective nuclear charge** | Basis | Nuclear charge (Z) | Effective nuclear charge (Z_eff) | |---|---|---| | Definition | Total proton count | Net pull after shielding: Z − σ | | Value | Fixed by the element | Less than Z; depends on the electron watched | | Changes across a…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Z_eff is electron-specific:** the inner 1s electrons of Na feel Z_eff ≈ +10.9, not +1 — always say *which electron* you are computing for.  ·  **Down a group Z grows but Z_eff does not:** the new shell's shielding cancels the extra protons; students who quote "Z increases so pull increases down a group" get the trend backwards.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Shielding vs penetration:** shielding is what *other electrons do to you*; penetration is how *close you get* despite them. s penetrates best and is least shielded.  ·  ## 7.
